confidence_notes: Food and drink prices come from three web searches. They draw on crowd-sourced cost-of-living figures (MyLifeElsewhere for Brno: local beer about 56 CZK, cappuccino about 73 CZK, inexpensive meal about 200 CZK; Expatistan for Brno: cocktail about 159 CZK, based on few data points and last updated mid-2025), a 2026 national Czech guide (Freenance: pub beer 45-75 CZK, cappuccino 60-90 CZK) and secondary reports of a mid-range three-course dinner for two at about 1,000 CZK, which were mostly Prague or national figures rather than Brno-specific. I raised prices slightly to allow for restaurant pricing and inflation to July 2026, and converted CZK at roughly 21-21.5 CZK per USD. The mid-range meal is less certain because I found no clean Brno-only figure. I found no aggregated Brno price for a glass of wine, so I based it on local bottle prices and its usual ratio to beer (about 1.6-1.8 times a draft beer). The cocktail figure is between the Expatistan club price and higher lounge prices. Accommodation figures are my own estimates from general knowledge for July, which is summer high season. I did not check any live listings. Brno also hosts large events, such as trade fairs and the MotoGP weekend, that can push rates up sharply on some dates.
comparable_city_reasoning: Brno is the Czech Republic's second city and is generally somewhat cheaper than Prague. Its prices are similar to other Central European regional cities such as Bratislava, Kraków and Wrocław, with hostel and three-star hotel rates below Prague's tourist-core levels.
